description: Hi everyone! We are a determined team of high-school students whose aim is to build a engaging interactive space game. We are passionate about space exploration and game development. We are looking for frontend/game devs, coders and UI/UX Graphic designers.
summary:
We built Outpost 3D, a browser-based 3D space habitat game for the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission" mission. In the game, you get to play as an astronaut trying to sustain a Moon or Mars base running by balancing oxygen, power, water, and food in real time while facing sudden environmental hazards.
To keep younger players from getting bogged down in boring spreadsheets or complicated menus, we designed a rotating 3D "Vitals" figure of your astronaut. When a resource runs low, the matching part of the astronaut's body turns red—giving kids an instant visual warning that every decision has a real consequence. We grounded our resource drain rates and closed-loop trade-offs in real NASA Environmental Control and Life Support System research and astronaut consumption data.
Outpost 3D matters because reading space facts in a textbook is easy to forget, while actually managing a crisis is compelling. By letting kids test real aerospace engineering trade-offs firsthand, it teaches systems thinking, resource conservation, and what it genuinely takes to survive on somewhere other than space.
details:
Outpost 3D is a browser-based 3D space habitat game we built for the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission" mission. In the game, you step into the role of an astronaut trying to keep a Moon or Mars base running. You have to manage essential life-support resources—oxygen, power, water, and food—in real time while dealing with sudden environmental problems. On the side of the screen, there is a rotating 3D "Vitals" figure of your astronaut. Whenever a resource runs low, the matching part of the astronaut's body turns red, giving you an instant visual warning that something is going wrong.

Most space education for kids relies on reading facts, which is easy to forget. We wanted kids to actually feel what it takes to survive off-Earth. In Outpost 3D, every decision has a real consequence—if you drain too much power on one system, oxygen production drops and your astronaut's vitals start failing. Our goal is to help younger players understand systems thinking, resource conservation, and why astronauts have to carefully balance every watt of electricity and drop of water.

Tools we used:
HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and WebGL/Three.js for the 3D graphics, and hosted live on Vercel. Following NASA Space Apps rules, we want to note that we used Claude to help write and debug parts of the code. Our team came up with the original concept, designed the 3D Vitals mechanic, structured the gameplay loop, and checked all the NASA data ourselves.
